what: Regeneron discovers and sells biologic medicines. Eylea for eye disease is its largest own product, and it shares the economics of Dupixent, the large inflammatory-disease medicine, with Sanofi.
customers: Health systems, insurers and government payers; medicines are prescribed by specialists.
money: injections for wet age-related macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease
its share of profits from the medicine marketed with Sanofi
Libtayo in cancer and newer launches
moat: Its VelociSuite antibody discovery platform, which has produced an unusual number of approved medicines, and deep manufacturing capability.
risks: Eylea faces biosimilar competition and sales have been falling
Revenue growth has stalled at about 1% in the last financial year
Much of its growth depends on a product it shares with a partner
Reimbursement decisions in the US affect the eye-disease franchise directly
opportunities: Eylea HD, the longer-acting version, can defend the franchise if uptake continues
Dupixent keeps adding new approved uses and growing strongly
It holds about $9 billion of cash against only $2 billion of debt, funding research and buybacks
watch: Combined Eylea and Eylea HD sales, and the first approvals from its newer oncology and obesity programmes.
